doc: Bringing repositories and agents onto the ontology, and growing it one increment at a time.
Inline links inside a boundary may only target the concepts its manifest allows, written or derived from what it declares; stepping outside is HARD.
A file or a declaration inside one; the subject of a link.
An architectural unit (domain, system, container, component) with a manifest that declares its capability.
Holding the code to the ontology: lint, drift between declared and derived, and the gate on a change, by the rules GlossMark enforces.
A named idea in a namespace; the object of a link.
How sure the author of a proposal is, in [0, 1].
The share of implementation concepts with at least one artifact and one verifier; the share of files with an accepted link is secondary.
How much review a concept or boundary deserves (low, medium, high or critical); a change that touches it inherits the gate its level demands.
A proposed concept nobody has defined, turned into a question for the namespace owner.
A link named a concept that does not exist yet, and the namespace owner is asked to define it or refuse it.
What a boundary's code derives must stay within what its manifest declares.
Disagreement between what a boundary declares and what its code derives.
Comparing what manifests declare with what rollup derives.
A boundary's code was found to derive something its manifest does not declare, or not to derive something it does.
Reading markers, manifests and ontology files out of a repository into the graph.
Classifying a change as AUTO, SOFT or HARD by the views it touches.
A comment-native code ontology: links written in comments, compiled into one graph that is checked, compared, gated and projected.
The canonical graph of artifacts, concepts, boundaries and the edges between them.
Which views a change alters, and therefore how hard its gate is.
A ticket, a spec or a bug curated into an ontology change first and implemented against it second: the unit of ontology-first engineering.
Several repositories' graphs joined by IRI.
The review state and provenance of every link.
The binding of an artifact to a concept; written as a marker in a comment.
A reviewer accepted a proposed link, or re-confirmed a stale one.
An agent or a tool proposed a link that awaits review.
A reviewer rejected a proposed link, with a reason.
An accepted link whose anchor changed underneath it.
Syntax, references, domain and range, tiers, allowed lists.
The model a repository is described in: artifacts, concepts in namespaces, boundaries, and the links between them.
The unit of modularity; owns concepts and a tier.
Bringing a repository under GlossMark: scaffolding it, importing the vocabulary it already keeps, and drafting its first links for review.
Importers extend, never mutate; a repo only asserts facts whose subject it owns.

A planned concept, or a manifest's planned declaration, that nothing implements yet: an orphan or a gap with a deadline and a kinder name. Drift reports it open, overdue past its date, or closed once code reaches it.
Showing the graph to its readers: views, the landscape across repositories, and what a namespace publishes.
Selecting and arranging part of the graph for one observer, by tier, zoom or feature.
A link an agent proposes and a human has not yet accepted.
Exposing a namespace's published concepts to importing repositories.
Only published concepts cross repositories, and touching one is HARD.
Compiling a repository's markers, manifests and ontology files into one graph, and deriving what they imply.
A typed edge with a domain, a range and lifting rules.
Deciding whether a proposed link or concept holds: accept it, reject it with a reason, or re-confirm a stale one. HARD decisions are a person's; the rest may be an agent's.
Deciding what agents and people propose, and keeping the record of every decision.
Deriving higher-level facts (containment, realization, lifting) from code-level links.
Core never mentions implementation; every implementation concept realizes a core concept or is internal.
A published value follows the code it is bound to; a change to that code alone is drift.
A projection of the graph over tier and zoom for one observer.
The concepts and relations served to coding agents while they write, as an AGENTS.md snippet or over MCP.

The staged adoption levels (ADR 0044, #258): adoption: in glossmark.yaml names the rung a repository has reached (0 vocabulary, 1 manifests, 2 criticality, 3 full) and caps what gloss check, drift and diff fail; gloss doctor reads the rung the tree has reached and names what the next one adds.
The adopt-glossmark, derive-ontology and review-glossmark Claude Code skills, shipped in the binary.

The agent benchmark (#271): tickets against the showcase repositories with the domain pitfalls each sets, the scorer that reads an agent's tree through the linter, the drift report and the gate, and the runner that compares agents with and without GlossMark context.

gloss hook install --agent: the ready-made Claude Code plugin, Cursor rule and Copilot instructions, each with its MCP config, that give an agent the briefing, the skills and the concept tools in one step; every file committed and running gloss by name.
The AGENTS.md vocabulary snippet and the session-start briefing.
The deterministic graph.jsonl record stream (nodes, then edges, with provenance) and its JSON-LD context.

gloss report compliance: for each rule or critical concept, the code that enforces it, the tests that verify it, its published value, every ledger decision about those links and the open findings and waivers, as Markdown, HTML, CSV or JSON for an auditor.
Stamps every concept, boundary and artifact with its effective criticality and reports boundaries that understate it.
Binding a marker to the declaration that follows it.
The default soft-conf-threshold: proposals at or above it are SOFT. Bound to DefaultPolicy by a publishes-value marker.
One-line setup checks, each with its fix.
Classifies each declared-versus-derived pair as consistent, a violation or a gap, adds the concept- and link-level findings (orphan, untested, stale and the rest) and computes coverage.
gloss harvest: evidence of a repository's vocabulary from code, schemas, tests, UI, docs and git, before it has an ontology, and the lexical clusters a derivation starts from (ADR 0025).
Pass 1; markers, manifests and ontologies into the graph.
The typed shapes of every file GlossMark reads or writes.
The tool release, grammar and on-disk format versions.
Classifies the changes between two graphs as AUTO, SOFT or HARD by the views and criticality they touch, and renders the PR impact.
The gloss command and the Go library it is built from.
Read-only browsing of the graph (gloss review node, the Browse tab, browse_node): any node with its edges in and out by relation and the drift findings on it.
The graph.jsonl record format docs/VERSIONING.md documents; bumping it in code without here is value drift.
The static page that shows a projection: a UI surface for views, not their mechanism.
Resolving import version ranges and pinning each import's version and content hash in glossmark.lock: the importer's side of the published seam.

The curate-increment skill: takes a ticket, spec or bug as evidence, interviews the owner (scope, processes, concepts, boundaries, seam, views, criticality), reviews the draft with them and writes the planned entries, manifest declarations, view and plan record. It writes no code or markers and stops before the PR.
Unions sibling repositories' graphs by IRI; realizes the landscape itself, there is no separate federation process yet.
Mapping the links: entries of manifests and glossmark.yaml onto code: a path glob at file scope, or a declaration symbol anchored as a marker above it would be (ADR 0045).
Where the tier, seam, own-subject and allowed-list constraints are enforced.
Parsing one marker line and the per-extension comment table.
gloss suggest: proposed links for unmarked public surfaces, from names, docstrings, the tables they touch and the code their tests call.
The MCP server agents call to search concepts, ask what a path or change touches, and propose links and concepts.
Formatting-preserving edits to ontology files: add, accept or remove a proposed concept and rewrite NEW markers once it exists.

The committed .glossmark/plan.jsonl, read and validated by gloss: one brief line per increment, one decision line per entry written or changed, one deviation line per departure. It keeps why each plan entry was written.
Per-namespace ontology.jsonld and graph.jsonl for importers.

gloss app serve (ADR 0052, #264): the hosted GitHub App that gates a pull request with no CI setup. It receives the pull_request webhooks, checks the PR out, runs the Gate against the merge base as the PR author and posts the impact comment the Action posts, a check run (action_required on HARD until a reviewer labels the PR ontology-approved) and a review request to the owners of the HARD changes (app.owners in glossmark.yaml, CODEOWNERS as the fallback). GitLab is a follow-up.

glossmark.yaml relations: starter | full. Under starter, check hints (GM250) at a relation outside the starter set and the agent surfaces list only it; the graph is the same under either (issue #261).
accept, reject and status.

gloss review (experimental, ADR 0033): the queue of everything that waits on a reviewer with the context each item needs, decisions by the gate's authority, recommendations, and an undo journal; headless as JSON and MCP.
The .glossmark/ledger.jsonl record of each link's review state, reviewer, reason and anchor fingerprint.
The full-screen terminal for gloss review: the queue beside an item's context, history and concepts, one key per decision, prompts for what it needs, undo.
Derives boundary-level facts from code-level links: containment, realization lifted to cores, flows lifted to boundaries, implied relationships.
gloss init: config, tier files, manifests, views, CI job and hook in one command.
gloss export --sqlite: the graph as a SQLite database with closure views, for ad-hoc queries.
gloss strip, the reverse of gloss init: a final export of the graph, ledger and ontology, then every marker, manifest and tool file removed from the tree, so a trial leaves no trace.

gloss suggest --eval, --calibrate and the calibration harness: precision and auto-accept rate per confidence band on labelled links, the counts conf is read from, and the auto-accept threshold derived from a precision target.
Unified diffs of ontology files, so a suggested edit is reviewable before it is written.
Resolves value-from and publishes-value to a line of code; the ledger baselines it and the comparator reports drift.
Builds the views ontology/views.yaml defines and feature slices from the graph.
gloss import: a markdown glossary or an enums file into an owned namespace, re-runnable.
Reading glossmark.yaml, ontology files, manifests and imports.
The concepts GlossMark exists to manage, independent of how the tool is built.
